blocks.en: Image restoration is a fundamental inverse problem that seeks to recover high-quality images from degraded observations. Plug-and-Play (PnP) methods provide a flexible framework for integrating pretrained denoisers into iterative reconstruction, whereas flow matching offers an efficient generative modeling approach based on continuous-time ODE dynamics. Very recently, Martin et al.\ (ICLR, 2025) developed a PnP-Flow method, which integrates the PnP framework with flow matching through a time-dependent denoiser constructed from a pretrained flow matching model.By incorporating a different time schedule and an additional pixel-space projection operator, this paper proposes a novel efficient PnP-Flow algorithm (HP-PnP-Flow) that enjoys rigorous convergence guarantees under mild assumptions, without imposing restrictive conditions on iterates required by the aforementioned work. Numerical experiments on CelebA and AFHQ-Cat demonstrate that the newly proposed HP-PnP-Flow algorithm significantly outperforms PnP-Flow on several restoration tasks such as denoising, deblurring, super-resolution, random inpainting, and box inpainting. Notably, our algorithm achieves comparable or better reconstruction quality with substantially fewer iterations, reducing the iteration count from $500$ to $100$ for deblurring and super-resolution on AFHQ-Cat.

Image restoration has been a long-standing problem in a wide range of applications, including digital photography, medical imaging, remote sensing, surveillance and digital entertainment [ 33 , 39 ] .
Given a degraded observation, the objective is to recover the underlying clean image, where the degradation may arise from various factors during image acquisition, transmission, or processing [ 23 , 31 , 15 , 14 , 22 ] .
Such restoration tasks can typically be formulated as inverse problems under the observation model y = H ​ x + ζ , y=Hx+\zeta, (1.1) where x ∈ ℝ d x\in\mathbb{R}^{d} denotes the unknown high-quality image, y ∈ ℝ m y\in\mathbb{R}^{m} is the degraded observation, H : ℝ d → ℝ m H:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{m} denotes the degradation operator, and ζ \zeta describes the underlying additive noise.
The inherent ill-posedness and high dimensionality of the problem pose significant challenges to accurate and stable reconstruction.

In recent years, the regularized minimization problem ( 1.3 ) has received considerable attention.
Early works addressed this problem by using proximal splitting methods, which handle the data-fidelity and regularization terms separately.
For example, forward-backward splitting (FBS) [ 4 , 10 ] alternates between a proximal operation on g g and a gradient descent step on f f , when f f is differentiable.
In more general settings, half-quadratic-splitting (HQS) [ 17 ] , alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) [ 2 ] or douglas-rachford splitting (DRS) [ 13 ] use proximal operations for both f f and g g .

Plug-and-Play (PnP) method. Since designing an effective regularizer for complex priors is challenging, the authors of [ 37 ] introduced the Plug-and-Play (PnP) methods, which replace the proximal operator with an off-the-shelf denoiser such as
DnCNN [ 43 ] or DRUNet [ 42 ] .
Over the last few years, much attention has been received on various PnP methods and their convergence analysis (see, e.g., [ 28 , 35 , 29 , 32 , 21 ] and references therein).
For example, the authors of [ 40 ] first provide a new convergence theory for plug-and-play proximal gradient descent (PnP-PGD) under prior mismatch where the denoiser is trained on a different data distribution to the inference task at hand.
By incorporating neural network denoisers, PnP methods have achieved promising results across various image restoration tasks.
However, classical PnP methods typically rely on generic discriminative denoisers, for which an explicit regularization function may not be available.
This limits both the optimization interpretation of the method and its ability to represent complex image distributions.

Generative models provide a natural alternative by modeling the underlying data distribution, and have achieved state-of-the-art performance in image generation, inverse problems and a broad range of related applications [ 12 , 19 , 34 , 9 , 5 , 25 , 26 ] . In particular, flow matching learns
a time-dependent vector field whose ODE flow transports
a base distribution to the data distribution.
Owing to simpler training objectives and more efficient sampling, flow matching has recently emerged as a powerful framework for continuous-time generative modeling.
These developments have motivated the use of generative models as image priors within the PnP framework.
Very recently, Martin et al. [ 27 ] introduced PnP-Flow matching method by defining a time-dependent denoiser using a pretrained flow matching model.
Under regularity assumptions and bounded support of the base distribution, they established convergence under the additional assumptions that the iterates remain bounded and the time sequence satisfies ∑ k = 0 ∞ ( 1 − t k ) < ∞ \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(1-t_{k})<\infty .

budget N N .
On the other hand, the convergence guarantee is obtained based on bounded iterates, a property that is not explicitly guaranteed by the original algorithm.

An improved HP-PnP-Flow algorithm. In this work, we address this problem by proposing a hybrid-projection PnP-Flow (HP-PnP-Flow) algorithm, based on a different time schedule and an additional
pixel-space projection operator.
More precisely, the hybrid time schedule given by ( 3.1 ) combines geometric and linear phases, while the projection operator defined by ( 3.2 ) explicitly constrains the iterates to the prescribed pixel range.
Under mild and reasonable assumptions,
we establish the convergence of HP-PnP-Flow (see Theorem 3.3 ), without requiring the a priori boundedness assumptions on the iterates imposed in the original PnP-Flow framework in [ 27 ] . Also, the new hybrid time schedule ensures the resulting time sequence satisfies the uniform boundedness assumption ∑ k = 0 ∞ ( 1 − t k ) < ∞ \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(1-t_{k})<\infty .
Notably, numerical experiments demonstrate the efficiency and high quality of the new algorithm.
Ablation studies further validate the individual effects of the initial time offset t 0 t_{0} and the hybrid time schedule, with their combination yielding the best overall performance.
In summary, our main contributions are as follows: • We propose an improved PnP-Flow algorithm, called HP-PnP-Flow, by incorporating a novel hybrid time schedule and an additional pixel-space projection operator. • We establish the convergence of the newly proposed HP-PnP-Flow algorithm under mild and reasonable assumptions. • Extensive experiments on two datasets and five tasks demonstrate that our algorithm significantly outperforms PnP-Flow in terms of reconstruction quality and convergence efficiency.

blocks.en:
In this section, we evaluate the performance of HP-PnP-Flow algorithm ( 3.3 ) on five canonical image restoration tasks, including denoising, deblurring, super-resolution, random-pixel inpainting, and box inpainting, using two publicly available datasets.
We compare our algorithm with several baseline methods using PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS, and perform ablation studies to assess the effects of the hybrid time schedule and the initial time offset.

我们用PSNR,SSIM,和LPIPS等几种基准方法来比较我们的算法,并进行衰减研究,以评估混合时间表和初始时间抵消的影响.

From Figure 5 , we observe that a larger K K accelerates early-stage convergence by increasing the contribution of the geometric phase.
The purely linear schedule ( K = 0 K=0 ) exhibits the slowest early-stage convergence, whereas larger values of K K lead to more rapid initial PSNR improvement.

blocks.en:
In this work, we propose an efficient hybrid-projection Plug-and-Play-Flow algorithm, an improved Plug-and-Play algorithm for image inverse problems that integrates flow matching priors with a hybrid time schedule and pixel-space projection operator.
Furthermore, we establish the convergence of HP-PnP-Flow without imposing the boundedness assumption on the iterates required in original PnP-Flow (see Proposition 4 in [ 27 ] ), since the pixel-space projection keeps the iterates within the prescribed pixel range.
The hybrid schedule combines geometric and linear growth phases, satisfies the convergence condition, and achieves faster early-stage reconstruction and improved numerical performance over the linear schedule used in PnP-Flow.
Experiments on CelebA and AFHQ-Cat across five degradation tasks show that HP-PnP-Flow achieves the best or second-best PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS in most settings, while requiring fewer iterations than PnP-Flow (e.g., 100 100 vs. 500 500 iterations for deblurring on AFHQ-Cat).
Ablation studies further demonstrate that the initial time offset t 0 t_{0} and the hybrid schedule contribute independently to the performance gains, with their combination yielding the best overall performance.
blocks.zh:
在这项工作中,我们提出一个高效的混合投影插图和Play-Flow算法,一个经过改进的用于图像反向问题的插图和Play算法,将流量匹配的前缀与混合时间表和像素空间投影操作员相结合.
此外,我们确定HP-PnP-Flow的趋同,而不对原始的PnP-Flow所需的远地点强加界限假设(见[27]中的提案4),因为像素-空间投影使远地点保持在规定的像素范围内.
混合式时间表结合了几何和线性增长阶段,满足了汇合条件,实现了比PnP-Flow所使用的线性时间表更快的早期重建并改进了数字性能.
在CelebA和AFHQ-Cat上的实验跨越了五个降解任务,表明HP-PnP-Flow在大多数情况下都实现了最佳或第二最佳的PSNR,SSIM,以及LPIPS,同时需要比PnP-Flow更少的迭代(例如,在AFHQ-Cat上脱落的100100对500次迭代).
校对研究进一步表明,初始时间抵消t 0 t_{0}和混合时间表独立地促进了绩效增益,两者的结合产生了最佳的整体绩效.

blocks.en:
Several directions remain for future investigation.
First, we plan to establish quantitative error bounds for HP-PnP-Flow under mild assumptions.
Second, it would be interesting to explore whether the proposed hybrid time schedule can be extended to other generative-model-based PnP frameworks beyond flow matching.
